Cancer problem in India 
1.7 The growing burden of cancer in India is a major healthcare issue. As per the 
International Agency for Research on Cancer GLOBOCAN project, it is expected that the burden 
of cancer in India will increase from an estimated incidence of 1.1 million cases in 2018 to about 
1.9 million in 2040. What is more alarming is that cancer deaths are expected to rise from 0.78 
million in 2018 to 1.3 million in 2040. The mortality: incidence ratio of 0.68 in India is far 
higher than that in very high human development index (HDI) countries (0. 38) and high HDI 
countries (0.57). While some of this disparity is because of over -diagnosis in more developed 
countries, it is also due to the unequal distribution of and lack of access to health care resources 
across India. Even among those who are able to access health care, survival is compromised by 
advanced stage at diagnosis and inability to afford optimum treatment. In addition to increasing 
awareness about cancer, augmenting infrastructure for cancer care and improving access to 
health care, one of  the key solutions is to increase the emphasis on research that can identify 
affordable, cost-effective interventions for the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of common 
cancers in India. Currently, there are very few government funded cancer centres pro viding high 
quality cancer care, education and research. 
National Cancer Control Programme 
1.8 Although the National Cancer Control Program me (NCCP) has been in place since 1975, 
it has not been impactful primarily because of the lack of political support in past years. We 
propose that the NCCP be revisited under the aegis of the National Cancer Grid, a flagship 
programme of the Government of I ndia. Primarily, the focus needs to continue on prevention of 
common cancers like those of the oral cavity, cervix, lung. Early detection by increasing 
awareness amongst the lay public as well as the primary care physician (including alternative 
medicine practitioners and traditional healers) needs to be at a priority. However, there is also the 
need for augmenting treatment facilities in various parts of the country. Currently, over     two-
thirds of cancer care is provided by private sector. Increasing co sts and out of pocket expenses , 
therefore, results in close to 6% of India‟s population going below the poverty line every year. 
There is an urgent need to augment the cancer care facilities in the country. In addition, attention 
is also required in the areas of palliative care, survivorship and patient advocacy. Data collection 
and aggregation, evaluating patterns of care, and health technology assessment are also required 
to channelize scarce healthcare resources appropriately. 
A dual approach is required  for planning a systematic National Cancer Plan . First, 
existing centres should be strengthened to provide uniform standards of cancer care across the 
country. Secondly, additional Government run cancer centres need to be set up to fill the gaps in 
access across several geographies. The first approach has been successfully done by the National 
Cancer Grid, a large network of cancer centres, research institutions, patient groups and 
professional societies, with the mandate of establishing uniform standards o f patient care for 
prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of cancer, creating adequate trained human resources, and 
facilitating collaborative basic, translational and clinical research in cancer. However, there is 
still a need to create additional government-run cancer centres which can provide affordable high 
quality cancer care to all sections of society. 
 
 

4 
 
Tata Memorial Centre (TMC) 
1.9 The Tata Memorial Centre, a grant -in-aid organization under the Department of Atomic 
Energy, is the oldest and largest cancer centre in the country. Registering close to 80,000 new 
patients and over 500,000 follow ups annually, it provides high quality cancer care to patients 
from across the country regardless of socio -economic status; more than 60% of patients are 
treated almost free of cost. TMC also is the centre for cancer education in the country and trains 
over 100 students every year in various aspects of cancer including surgical, medical and 
radiation oncology. Research from TMC has addre ssed several important questions and changed 
cancer practice globally. ACTREC is the research wing of TMC and houses several cancer 
researchers working towards unravelling the biology, causes and management of cancer. In 
addition, TMC has now expanded to s ix other hospitals located in Varanasi (two), Guwahati, 
Sangrur, Vishakapatnam and Mullanpur. It is expected that TMC will treat over 150,000 new 
patients with cancer annually by the year 2022. 
The National Cancer Grid 
1.10 The National Cancer Grid, an ini tiative of the Department of Atomic Energy, 
Government of India, was created in 2012 with the broad vision of creating uniform standards of 
cancer care across India. Seven years later, it has grown to a large network of 238 cancer centres, 
research institutes, patient advocacy groups, charitable organizations and professional societies. 
Between the member organizations of the NCG, the network treats over 700,000 new patients 
with cancer annually, which is over 60% of all of India‟s cancer burden. Incorporat ing all 
stakeholders of cancer care in India, it is a strong, unified and powerful voice in the fight against 
cancer. 
NCG activities include the following: 
1. Uniform standards of care – NCG Consensus Guidelines 
2. External Quality Assurance Schemes (EQAS) 
3. Second opinion service for patients – “Navya” 
4. NCG Virtual Tumor Boards 
5. Price Discovery Cell / Group negotiation for equipment, drugs and consumables 
6. Continuing Medical Education – NCG National Cancer Library and Discovery tool 
“Akshara” 
7. Unique Educational Initiatives – “Traveling Schools of Pathology and Oncology 
Nursing” 
8. Training in Cancer Research Methods – International Collaboration on Research methods 
Development in Oncology – CreDO workshop 
9. NCG funded multicentric collaborative research 
Hub and spoke model of cancer care 
1.11 A distributed model of cancer care is required to offer patients high quality cancer care at 
their doorsteps. Common and less complex cancer care should be provided close to patients‟ 
homes (spokes) to create minimum disruption in  their lives and that of their families. Treatment 
of uncommon cancers and those with complex treatment protocols require management in expert 
centres of excellence (hubs). However, to avoid over -burdening the hubs, the spokes need to be 
reasonably capable  of handling less complex and common cancer types in the region. This 
strategy would be extremely helpful to minimize costs as well as inconvenience to patients and 
their families. We suggest a comprehensive cancer plan which will address the increasing burden 
of cancer in India by the creation of approximately 30 hubs and 120 spokes in various parts of 
the country. 
Suggested approach 
1.12 Tata Memorial Centre, a grant-in-aid tertiary cancer hospital under Department of 
Atomic Energy, Government of India has been offering state of the art cancer services for last 80 
years. We strive for excellence in cancer care, education, research, public health since our 

5 
 
inception. We hav e now set up hospitals in Sangrur, Chandigarh, Varanasi, Vishakhapatnam, 
Guwahati and Muzaffarpur. While the hospitals in Sangrur, Guwahati, Varanasi are fully 
functional, the facilities in Chandigarh and Vishakhapatnam will be fully commissioned by the 
end of this year. We also offered technical assistance to the Uttar Pradesh ( UP) Government in 
setting up State Cancer Institute at Lucknow.  
It is agreed upon that the availability of affordable cancer care is not uniformly available 
in all geographical areas of our vast country. It is ideal to establish TMC‟s hub and spoke model 
in such a way that no patient has to travel more than three hours to access basic cancer care. The 
model has been endorsed by the Parliamentary Committee on Science and Technology i n its 
report on improving cancer care and control in India. The National Cancer Grid is another 
initiative to standardize cancer care all across the nation.

funds, and statutory permissions are in place.  A typical spoke is a 100 bedded facility that takes 
care of nearly two thirds of the cancer care spectrum. The approximate cost of setting up a spoke 
is approximately Rs 385 crore and it can be commissioned in 2 -4 years after approvals, sanction

1. West Bengal - We suggest that TMC provide technical assistance to an existing facility in

2. Chhattisgarh – On the request of forme r Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh, our team has

3. Goa: As per our assessment, the region around Karwar is deficient in good cancer 
hospitals in the vi cinity. Karwar would be a good site for a spoke as it can service 
patients from Goa as well as North Karnataka. Given the close proximity of Kaiga, this 
can be an appropriate site for a hub to be built by DAE in partnership with the State 
Government. 
4. Odisha: We are aware of an ongoing effort to establish a large cancer centre at 
Bhubhaneswar by the Odisha State Government; in addition, there is a regional cancer 
centre at Cuttack, and an AIIMS in Bhubhaneswar. It would be best that we offer 
technical assist ance to the State Government in their existing proposal of creating a 
cancer centre, which would be a hub. An annual expenditure of Rs 30 crore would be 
required to support infrastructure/ equipment upgrade and operation expenses. 
5. Rajasthan: Southern Rajas than has a scarcity of cancer centres and hence, Udaipur or 
Kota would be good choices to create hubs of cancer care. This would be a greenfield 
project with the creation of a hub. 
As mentioned above, there are two different models being proposed. In the f irst scenario, 
(West Bengal, Chattisgarh, Odisha), TMC will offer technical assistance (civil work planning, 
architectural planning, guidance on equipment purchase, human resource recruitment and 
commissioning) to an existing or upcoming facility for upgradation to a Hub or a spoke. It would 
be preferable to have the location of this facility in an existing government hospital or a 
charitable hospital. In this case, most of the capital cost will be borne by the relevant stakeholder, 
while there may be some supplementary funding for operational expenditure and upgradation of 
infrastructure / equipment from the DAE. In the second scenario (Karwar, Kota/Udaipur and any 
of the above -mentioned sites where collaboration with the suggested centres does not 
materialize), TMC would plan to establish and run the facility itself as a greenfield project. All 
facilities will be functionally and academically autonomous, run directly by TMC.

SEWAGE SLUDGE HYGIENISATION  
Recommendation/Observation  
3.1 The Committee appreciates the Department for developing an indigenous technology for 
hygienisation of municipal sewage sludge. The Committee, however, finds it surprising that 
though this technology is scientifically sound, it has not been promoted to the desired level and 
only a handful of Municipalities have shown interest in the technology. The Committee is of the 
opinion that this technology can be used on a larger scale by the other Municipalities in the 
country to tackle the problem of sewage sludge.  The Committee is of the considered view that 
the success in Ahmedabad may be replicated across all the major Municipalities in the country, 
in a phased manner, and the Municipalities finding it difficult to deal with its sewage sludge 
should come forward and make best use of this technology. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Department should write to all State/UT Governments, apprise them the 
benefits and efficacy of this technology and ask them to impress upon all the Municipalities 
facing the problem of sewage sludge to use this technology to solve the problem faced by them.

The Action Taken Report (ATR) of the Committee deals with the action taken by the 
Government on the recommendations/observations contained in the Three Hundred Forty Second 
Report of the Committee on „Demands for Grants (202 1-22) of the „Department of Biotechnology‟. 
The Report was presented to Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on the 8th March, 2021.  
2. Action Taken Notes (ATN) have been received from the Department of Biotechnology‟ (DBT) 
in respect of the recommendations/observation s contained in the Three Hundred Forty Second Report. 
This has been categorized as follows:-  
Chapter I: Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the Government: 
Para Nos.:- 2.3, 2.3, 3.5, 3.7, 3.9, 3.10, 5.3, 6.2, 7.5, 8.2, 8.4, 8.5, 8.7, 8.9, and 8.10 
(of the Three Hundred Forty Second Report) 
  Total recommendations – 15 accepted. 
  The Committee is pleased to note that the Department has accepted its 
recommendations/observations as mentioned in Chapter-I of the Report. 
Chapter II:    Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue 
in view of the Government’s replies: Nil 
Chapter III: Recommendations/Observations in respect of which replies of the Government 
have not been accepted by the Committee: Nil 
Chapter IV:  Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the Government 
are still awaited:- Nil 
3. The details of the ATR have been analyzed in the succeeding Chapters.  

2 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
GOVERNMENT 
BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2020 -21 AND ALLOCATION FOR 
2021-22 
Recommendation/observation 
1.1  The Committee recognises that the Department has been able to utilise over 75 percent of the 
funds allotted during R.E. 2020 -21 upto 31.01 .2021. The Committee appreciates the overall fund 
utilsation by the Department in the recent past and urges the Department to fully utilise the funds by 
the end of the financial year.                                                                       (Para 2.3 of the 342nd Report)                                                                                                                             
Action Taken 
1.2 The Department of Biotechnology (DBT)  gratefully acknowledges the appreciation of the 
Committee.  It is submitted that out of the total allocation of Rs.2300 crore in RE 2020 -21, the total 
utilisation of funds by the end of the financial year was Rs.2266.45 crore which is 98.54% of the total 
RE allocations. 
CENTRAL SECTOR SCHEMES OF THE DEPARTMENT 
Recommendation/observation 
1.3 The Committee notes with satisfaction that the allocation wa s increased at the R.E. 2020 -21 
stage under the Central Sector Scheme –‘Industrial and Entrepreneurship Development’ under which 
the Department is implementi ng the crucial programs related to mitigation of COVID -19 pandemic. 
The Committee wishes that the Department will continue and further strengthen the initiatives taken by 
it under these schemes.                                                                                                         (Para 3.3ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.4 The observation of the Committee is noted. It is submitted that  besides the initiatives already 
under implementation, under the Industrial and Entrepreneurship Development (IED) sc heme, the 
Department of Biotechnology has launched „Mission COVID Suraksha -The Indian COVID -19 
Vaccine Development Mission‟, following due approval of the Expenditure Finance Committee and 
the Ministry of Finance, Government of India.  
1.5 The Mission was launched as part of the third stimulus package, Atmanirbhar Bharat 3.0, for 
promoting research and development of Indian COVID -19 vaccines. Mission COVID Suraksha is 
being implemented by Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), a Public Sector 
Undertaking (PSU) of DBT, at a total cost of Rs. 900 Cr. for 12 months. The goal of the Mission is to 
accelerate the development of at least 5-6 COVID-19 vaccine candidates and ensure that some of these 
are brought closer to licensure and introducti on in public health systems. Support is being provided 
under the Mission for candidate vaccines in clinical development, as well as, for strengthening the 
vaccine development ecosystem. As observed by the Committee, focused efforts will be made to 
further strengthen the initiative and contribute to the mitigation of the pandemic. 
Recommendation/observation 
1.6 The Committee hopes that with the increased allocation of Rs. 3502.37 crore in B.E. 2021 -22, 
the Department will be able to regain the momentum lost due to COVID -19 pandemic in the 
implementation of some of its schemes and new initiatives, and shall utilise its resources judiciously to 

3 
 
augment research and development, human resource capacity building, identify and support the start -
up ecosystem and strengthening initiatives for fighting COVID-19.                                   (Para 3.5ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.7 With the budget allocated for FY 2021 -22, the Department would be able to implement all 
major ongoing activities and would also augment the act ivities in the areas of research and 
development, Human Resource Development and translation research & entrepreneurship. The 
Department will continue to support the ecosystem for S&T solutions to fight COVID-19.   
Recommendation/observation 
1.8  The Commi ttee notes and appreciates the initiative of the Department towards ensuring the 
timely development of COVID-19 Vaccine for the nation.                                                  (Para 3.7 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.9 The Department acknowledges the apprec iation of the Committee. Development of COVID -19 
Vaccines is a priority area for the Department of Biotechnology, whereby, the Department has been 
identified as the Central co -ordinating agency for the PMO constituted Task force on Vaccines. Both 
national efforts and international partnerships are being leveraged for vaccine development and 
manufacturing. Several projects of industry and academia for development of vaccines candidates for 
COVID-19 and associated resources are being supported by DBT under th e DBT-BIRAC COVID-19 
Research Consortium. To strengthen and accelerate these efforts further, the Department has launched 
“Mission COVID Suraksha –The Indian COVID -19 Vaccine Development Mission” for ensuring that 
at least few of these vaccine candidates ar e brought closer to licensure and introduction in the market 
for consideration of regulatory authorities and for introduction in public health systems.  Five vaccine 
candidates in clinical development stage are being supported under the Mission.  Further, as part of the 
efforts to strengthen the vaccine development ecosystem , support is being provided for03 
immunogenicity assay laboratories and 03 animal challenge facilities. Also, 19 clinical trial sites across 
the nation are being supported to facilitate quick initiation of clinical trials for vaccine candidates. 
Recommendation/observation 
1.10   The Committee notes with utmost concern that details of the activities planned to be undertaken 
by the Department with the increased allocation for creation of Cap ital assets are not available in the 
documents furnished by the Department and break -up of budgetary allocations for Revenue and 
Capital Expenditure as well as funds allotted for Establishment Expenditure under various Budgetary 
Heads.  Without the above i nformation, the Committee is constrained in analysing the spend on new 
infrastructure and research. The Committee recommends that the Department should invariably 
furnish the above information to the Committee to facilitate analysis of Demands for Grants, and 
recalibrate the outcomes and outputs based on the complete Departmental funding.        (Para 3.9 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.11 A copy of the Statement of Budget Estimates (SBE) is annexed at Annexure -I. The 
recommendations made by the Committee have been noted for compliance. 
Recommendation/observation  
1.12 The Committee further recommends that the Department should immediately take up the matter 
with the concerned authorities and explore the possibility of bringing the necessary changes in the 
classification of allocation of funds under revenue and capital expenditure.                   (Para 3.10 ibid)                                                                                              
Action Taken 
1.13 The recommendations made by the Committee has been noted for compliance. 

4 
 
MAJOR INITIATIVES OF THE DEPARTMENT FOR FY 2021-22 
Mission COVID Suraksha 
Recommendation/observation 
1.14 The Committee notes the response of the Department and recommends the Department to 
strengthen on its part, the efforts f or ramping up the production capacity of the two approved vaccines 
as well as provide all research, laboratory infrastructure and capacity building support to the other 
vaccine candidates in the pipeline, in order to ensure the availability of a safe, affo rdable, and 
efficacious vaccine to the wider population as soon as possible.                                        (Para 5.3 ibid) 
 Action Taken 
1.15 The recommendation of the Committee has been noted.  Under Mission COVID Suraksha, the 
Department of Biot echnology is providing financial support to augment the vaccine production 
capacities. Accordingly, support for one private industry and three public sector manufacturing 
facilities, viz., Bharat Biotech, Hyderabad; Indian Immunologicals, Hyderabad; Haffki ne 
Biopharmaceuticals, M umbai and  Bharat Immunologicals and Biologicals, Bulandshar; is being 
provided to make them ready for enhanced capacities to support augmented vaccine production over 
the next 6 -8 months. It is expected that the current manufacturin g of Covaxin of 10 million doses/ 
month will be enhanced to nearly 100 million doses/ month in the next 8 -10 months. An amount of ~ 
Rs. 200 Cr. has been allocated for supporting augmentation of capacities for manufacturing. 
BIOTECH URJIT CLUSTER 
Recommendation/observation 
1.16 The Committee impresses upon the Department the need to have orientation, clear focus and 
seamless framework for translation of research outcomes into technologies, products and services that 
may be used by the Industries, SMEs, Entre preneurs and citizens at large. The Committee appreciates 
the initiative taken by the Department and extends its full support to this endeavour of the Department.       
                                                                                                                                             (Para 6.2 ibid)                                                                                  
Action Taken 
1.17 The Department gratefully acknowledges appreciation from the Committee. The Department 
has been implementing a program on “Accelerated Translational Grant for Commercialization 
(ATGC)” to promote the translation research and industry -academia partnership in biotechnology. 
Biotechnology Industry Research Assitance Council (BIRAC), a Public Se ctor Undertaking of the 
Department, over the past 9 years of its existence, has been able to support product and technology 
development from academia, start -ups and industries which has led to market launch of nearly 200+ 
products/technologies. The funding  schemes and programs have been designed to have focus on 
supporting transition of    Products & Technologies from ideation stage (Technology Readiness 
Level-1 i.e. TRL -1) to Proof of Concept (TRL -3) to Extensive Validation/Trials  (TRL -7), finally 
leading to market launch & commercialization (TRL -8&9). BIRAC has been providing mentorship 
with the help of domain experts at every stage of the project. By facilitating connection with right 
partners, providing regulatory guidance and follow -on funding for succ essful projects working on 
potential technologies/products, BIRAC has been able to support translation of ideas & prototypes 
into validated market-ready products.  
 
 
 

5 
 
TECHNOLOGY CLUSTER 
Recommendation/observation 
1.18 The Committee recognises the need for extending all possible support in terms of resources, 
technology, infrastructure and creating opportunities for growth for budding start -ups and 
entrepreneurs as well as for SMEs. The Committee appreciates the initiative of the Department and 
recommends th e Department should accelerate the process of identification of priority sectors and 
selection of location for setting up T -Clusters. The Committee also recommends that the Department 
should ensure equitable geographical distribution of these Technology Cl usters, so that the benefits of 
this initiative can reach the underserved regions of the country as well.                           (Para 7.5 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.19 The Committee‟s support for this initiative is greatly appreciated. Technology Clusters ar e 
expected to cater to the following sectors based on the experts and stakeholders feedback. Among this 
list, top 3 sectors shall be taken up on priority: 
o Medtech Devices and Diagnostics 
o Biopharma  
o Agritech & allied areas  
o Industrial Biotech 
o Clean Energy 
1.20 The department has undertaken a landscaping activity of Indian States to study biotech cluster 
potential. A formal report entitled “Realising Investment Potential for Indian State -Specific Biotech 
Industries” has been recently released. These inputs ar e important to gauge local potential, national 
priorities together with policy and incentives level support at State level to promote biotech ecosystem 
and shall assist in identif ication and prioritization of Technology Clusters seeding across the country.  
Subject to resource allocation, the activity will be expedited for implementation. 
AUTONOMOUS INSTITUTIONS OF THE DEPARTMENT 
Recommendation/observation 
1.21   The Committee recommends that the Department make judicious use of the revised allocations 
for 2 020-21 by prioritising the available resources and ensuring full utilisation of funds. The 
Committee also recommends the Department to make efforts to generate internal budgetary resources 
and try to offset the reduction in budgetary allocation.                                                      (Para 8.2 ibid)                                                                                                
Action Taken 
1.22 The Department utilized the revised allocation for FY 2020 -21 judiciously and utilized 98.54% 
of the revised allocation. The DBT Autonomous Institutions have been making efforts to generate 
internal budgetary resources.   
Recommendation/observation 
1.23 The Committee notes the contribution of the Autonomous Institutions under the Department and 
extends its heartfelt appreciation to the scientists, researchers, etc. working in the Department of 
Biotechnology and its affiliated institutions for their invaluable efforts/contribution towards 
strengthening the nation’s fight against COVID -19 pa ndemic.  The Committee further recommends 
upgrading infrastructure to address the gaps in BSL3/4 capabilities to further improve both 
diagnostics and research on new pathogens.                                                                      (Para 8.4 ibid) 
             
                                                                                       

6 
 
Action Taken 
1.24 The Department , along with its Autonomous Institutions , acknowledges gratefully the 
observations of the Committee. The Autonomous Ins titutions i.e. NII, ICGEB, In  Stem, ILS, RCB, 
THSTI of the Department have BSL 3 laboratories. Further, the Department is working on upgrading 
these facilities and also creating new facilities – BSL4/BSL-3.  
Recommendation/observation 
1.25 The Committee also recommends that the Department should impress upon all the Autonomous 
Institutions to enlist 10 goals/objectives that each of these laboratories propose to pursue in the 
medium to long term plan. The Autonomous Institutions should further indicate the g oals/objectives 
that will be pursued during the year 2021 -22 along with the steps that the Department plans to 
undertake to achieve these goals during the year.   On its part, the Department of Biotechnology 
should also develop a mechanism to periodically monitor the progress of the goals/objectives of each 
of these Autonomous Institutions.                                                                                        (Para 8.5 ibid) 
Action taken 
1.26 The recommendations of the Committee have been n oted for compliance. The goals/objectives 
of DBT Autonomous Institutions are annexed at Annexure - II.  
Recommendation/observation 
1.27 The Committee notes the efforts made by the Department for revenue generation and 
recommends that the Department should explore further avenues to augment revenue generation 
through technology transfer, consultancy services, patents, etc. The Committee recommends that the 
Department should actively reach out to the private sector and disseminate information about the 
technologies/products/services developed by the Department. On its part , the Department should also 
set targets for the same and actively monitor the progress.                                                (Para 8.7 ibid)                                                                       
Action Taken 
1.28 The Department has noted the recommendations of Committee. Actions   have been taken to 
augment revenue generation through technology transfer, consultancy services, Patents, etc. by the 
Autonomous Instituti ons of the Department.   BIRAC has launched the Biotech e -portal 
http://www.biotech-solutions.com showcases commercialized 150+ technologies, products from 
Startups to create awareness and attract stakeholders to support startups in the growth and scale up.  For 
COVID-19 related solutions, BIRAC has periodically taken out compendium to showcase Startup 
solutions that has led to their recognition and growth.    International mega events like Global Bio -India 
organized by DBT/BIRAC along with industry bodies CII , Invest India, ABLE provide exposure and 
opportunities like New Product Launch by Startups at international platform; Social media 
communications on Twitter, success story features on „ Vigyan se Vikas ‟  which shall be augmented 
further to monitor the outcome.  The Autonomous Institutions of the Department are being promoted to 
create industrial collaborations and also to offer consultancy services. Further, policy for user charges 
for high end equipment and for services to stakeholder, technology transfer are also framed by the 
Autonomous Institutions.    
Recommendation/observation 
1.29 The Committee recommends that the Department should resolve all the administrative issues 
which have held up the release of the second instalment of the Grant and release th e funds allocated 
for the Pune Biocluster, at the earliest.                                                                               (Para 8.9 ibid) 
 
            

7 
 
Action Taken 
1.30 As per the direction of Hon‟ble Minister of Science & Technology, the SFC note on 
Establishment of a Pune Biotech Cluster “Model Organisms to Human Disease” is being processed for 
the approval of the Competent Authority. 
Recommendation/observation 
1.31 The Committee strongly urges the Department to explore deeper into developi ng cure for 
certain rare diseases, for which the country is, by and large, dependent on imports and the patients 
have to shell out exorbitant amount of money for the cost and a sizeable amount on their excise/import 
duty.                                                                                                                                    (Para 8.10 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.32 The recommendations of the Committee have been noted. The Department has been supporting 
the several research proposals on development of bio-better therapeutics for rare and genetic disorders.

been at the forefront of genetic diagnostics and research in rare diseases for the past 25 years.

REPORT 
 
The Action Taken Report (ATR) of the Committee deals with action taken by the Government 
on recommendations/observations contained in the Three Hundred Forty Third Report of the 
Committee on „Demands for Grants (202 1-22) of the „Department of Scientific and Industrial 
Research‟ which was presented to Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on the 8th March, 
2021.  
2. Action Taken Notes (ATN) have been received from the Department of Scientific and Industrial 
Research‟ ( DSIR) in respect of the  recommendations/observations contained in the Three Hundred 
Forty Third Report. This has been categorized as follows:-  
Chapter I: Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the Government: 
Para Nos. 2.3, 2.7, 2.14, 4.3, 5.2, 6.3, 6.4, 6.6, 6.8, 6.10 and 7.3  
 Total recommendations – 11. Accepted 
The Committee is pleased to note that the Department has accepted its 
recommendations/observations as mentioned in Chapter-I of the Report. 
Chapter II:    Recommendations/Observations which the Commi ttee does not desire to pursue 
in view of the Government’s replies: Nil 
Chapter III: Recommendations/Observations in respect of which replies of the Government 
have not been accepted by the Committee: Nil 
Chapter IV:  Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the Government 
are still awaited: 
Para:- 2.9,  2.11, 2.13, 2.16 and 3.3 
Total recommendations –  5. To be pursued further 
The Committee desires that the Department should furnish pointed and detailed 
Action Taken Notes in respec t of recommendations/observations made in all chapters 
of the Report. 
3. The details of the ATR have been analyzed in the succeeding Chapters.

BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2020-21 AND ALLOCATION  
FOR 2021-22 
Recommendation/observation 
1.1 The Committee observes that the Department has been able to utilise over 90 percent of funds 
alllocated during R.E. 2020 -21 upto 31.01.2021. The Committee is satisfied with util isation of funds 
and hopes that the Department would be able to ensure its full utilisation by the end of financial year.                             
                                                                          (Para 2.3of the 343rd Report) 
Action Taken 
1.2 Details about the financial performance of the Department duri ng 2020-21 with details of B.E., 
R.E. and utilization of funds up to 31.03.2021 across its various schemes  is given in Annexure 1.  
Department has fully utilized the funds allocated during R.E. 2020-2021 for the F.Y. 2020-21. 
Recommendation/observation 
1.3 The Committee urges the Department to ensure full utilisation of funds allocated at R.E. 2020 -
21, especially under research and development initiatives under IRD, develops a robust  mechanism to 
achieve 100% coverage of timely disbursement of fellowships and finance projects undertaken by the 
two Public Sector Enterprises under the Department.  The Committee also recommends the 
Department to raise internal budgetary resources and try  to offset the reduction in budgetary 
allocation.                                                                           (Para 2.7 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.4 The Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR)  notes the concern of the 
Committee regarding full utilization of funds allocated at R.E. 2020 -21. DSIR Umbrella Scheme 
1 – Industrial Research and Development ( IRD) (which includes Common Research and 
Technology Development Hubs ( CRTDH), Patent Acquisition and Collaborative  Research & 
Technology Development   (PACE), Promoting Innovations in Individuals , Startups & MSMEs  
(PRISM) & Access to Knowledge  for Technology Development and Dissipation  (A2K+), have  
utilized 99.992% of the funds allocated in RE 2020 -21. DSIR Umbrella Scheme 2 –[National 
Research and Development Corporation ( NRDC) & Central Electronics Limited (CEL)] have utilized 
100 % of the funds allocated in RE 2020 -2021. For timely disbursal of fellowships, an end-to-end 
software, "NewFMS, has been developed by Council of Scientific and Industrial Research -National 
Chemical Laboratory ( CSIR-NCL) and implemented in the Council of Scientific and Industrial    
Research - Human Research Development Centre ( CSIR-HRDG) with effect from 01.04.2021. 
 Improvements in the software to address user feedback, security audit observations and opportunities 
for enhanced productivity are being carried out on a continuous basis." 
1.5 National Research Development Corporation ( NRDC) has undertaken 10 projects under 
Techno-commercial support and 6 projects u nder Priority Development Areas (PDAs) for further 
development of technologies.  Besides , the NRDC had also undertaken value -addition of 50 
technologies developed at various R&D institutes .

UMBRLLA SCHEME 2 – ASSISTANCE TO PSEs (National Research Development 
Corporation – NRDC and Central Electronics Limited –CEL) 
Recommendation/observation 
1.9 The Committee appreciates the role of NRDC in acting as a bridge between lab research and 
its translation into products by MSMEs. The Committee recommends that more aggressive steps be 
taken by the Department towards integration of entrepreneurs, SMEs and other private entities with 
the objective of translating R&D results into marketable products.                                  (Para 5.2 ibid)                                                   
Action Taken 
1.10 In order to further promote the translation o f R&D into marketable products, the NRDC 
has taken -up a new activity for providing support to the technology from “Proof of Concept 
(POC) stage ” to pre -commercialization and then upto commercialization stage. Besides , the 
Corporation would also organize se ctor specific Industry Interaction meets where the MSME‟s 
would be informed regarding the various technologies available in their area of operation . 
COUNCIL OF SCIENTIFIC AND INDUSTRIAL RESEARCH (CSIR) 
Recommendation/observation 
1.11 The Committee recommen ds that the Department should also explore raising extra budgetary 
resources to finance the establishment expenditure.                                           (Para 6.3 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.12 CSIR is trying to enhance its budgetary resource s through (i) Approaching Industries for 
seeking Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funding; (ii) Increasing its technology transfer 
and their commercialization   
Recommendation/observation 
1.13 The Committee is of the considered view that the avenues for translatio n of technology and 
commercialisation of research need  to be further augmented.  The Committee recommends that CSIR 
should take into account the requirements of the industries and work towards bridging the gap between 
what is required by the industry and w hat the institutes provide.  For this purpose, the Department 
should impress upon all the CSIR laboratories to enlist 10 goals/objectives that each of these 
laboratories propose to pursue in the medium to long term plan. The CSIR laboratories should furthe r 
indicate the goals/objectives that will be pursued during the year 2021 -22 along with the steps that the 
Department plans to undertake to achieve these goals during the year. On its part, Department of 
Scientific and Industrial Research should also devel op a mechanism to periodically monitor the 
progress of the goals/objectives of each of these laboratories.                                         (Para 6.4 ibid) 
Action Taken  
1.14 CSIR will follow the recommendations of the Committee for enhancing extra budgetary 
resources through appropriate steps to increase its technology translation and fulfilling the needs of the 
industries. In order to bridge the gap between CSIR and industries, a Committee was constituted  to:                
(i) Deliberate on all aspects related to “Ease of doing Science and Technology Business” in CSIR ; and 
(ii) Evolve facilitative models and enabling mechanisms to enhance “Ease of doing Science and 
Technology Business” in CSIR. The Committee deliberated upon intricacies of doing sc ience and 
technology business in CSIR keeping focus on: (a) CSIR Industry partnership, (b) Mechanisms by 
which Technology Readiness Levels can be improved faster, (c) Enhancing and enabling support 
system for pursuing S&T activities, and (d) Connecting with the stakeholders seamlessly. 
1.15 The major recommendations of the Committee in terms of connecting with different 
stakeholders are: (i) Synergizing with industry; (i i) Enabling and Robust Financial Systems;                      

5 
 
(iii) Strengthening & Promoting Entrepreneurship; (iv) Technical Innovation Centers (TICs) for Faster 
Product Development and Innovation Parks for Connecting with Industry ; and (v) Boosting Innovation 
& Technology Development and Commercialization.  Moving with aforesaid recommenda tions, the 
goals /objectives to pursue in the medium and long term as envisaged are as follows:  
(a). Understanding the R&D road map of prominent industries (big players as well as 
MSMEs) & mapping & aligning them to specific CSIR labs. 
(b). Tuning CSIR labs to seek and engage with industry at the incipient stage of an industry 
R&D project. 
(c). Evolve methodology for sharing of resources such as capital, Human Resources, assets, 
materials, etc. along with risk sharing. 
(d). Tuning organizational behavior and associated cultural changes (long term). 
(e). Enticing and educating Industry Captains/ Chief Executive Officer s (CEOs) to fund 
R&D in CSIR Labs. 
(f). Handholding industry (including Micro Small and Medium Enterprises). 
(g). The approach to building a p rofitable CSIR Technology Business for spin offs (long 
term). 
(h). Setting Up Pilot plants & facilities for scaling up in collaboration with Industries.  
(i). Co-locating Industry R&D labs in CSIR labs. 
(j). To improve efficiencies, utilization of funds co ming from non -governmental 
stakeholders such as industry, private charitable and scientific organizations and 
multi-lateral funding agencies shall be determined either by negotiated terms of 
agreements or, where not adequately specified in an agreement, by  the concerned 
laboratory Director for institute contracts or by Director General, CSIR for 
headquarters contracts without the requirement of following the General Financial 
Rules. 
Recommendation/observation 
1.16 The Committee notes the contribution of the  CSIR laboratories/institutes under the Department 
and extends its heartfelt appreciation to the scientists, researchers, etc. working in the Department of 
Scientific and Industrial Research for their invaluable effort and contribution towards strengthenin g 
the nation’s fight against COVID-19 pandemic.                                                                (Para 6.6 ibid)                                                  
Action Taken 
1.17 Department thankfully acknowledges the appreciation expressed by the Standing 
Committee towards the CSIR/DSIR efforts in fight against COVID -19 pandemic. Further to what 
has been achieved, CSIR is doing sequencing of corona genome at large scale to know about 
mutations happening in the country; post -vaccination immun e surveillance to assess the 
generation of antibodies including neutralizing antibodies; development of mRNA Vaccine 
Platform for vaccines and therapeutics; other vaccines for coronavirus based on new 
technologies; development of air purification system to  be installed in buses, metro rail, railways, 
auditoriums, hospitals and public places; development of air sampler to assess the presence of 
viable Corona Virus in air at public places and hospitals, clinical trials of new drugs etc. Robotic 
line of Feluda  has been developed by Tatas based on CSIR technology which can do 4000 
tests/day. These technologies will help the country in a big way in its fight against Corona Virus.

and outreach activities and showcase the technologies/products developed by it on more platforms so

also definitely lessen our dependency on imports of such products.                                   (Para 6.8 ibid)

1.19 Department would like to inform the Committee that following web portals have been 
launched for promotion of its technologies/produ cts and its outreach activities:

Recommendation/Observation

against the RE of Rs. 5012.10 crore, which amounts to 98% expenditure vis-à-vis Revised

the outcomes and physical targets of the Central Sector Schemes. The Committee, therefore,

Recommendation/Observation  
1.24 The Committee notes the economic, social, technological and developmental potential that 
lies in liberalisation and democ ratisation of the guidelines on acquisition and use of Geo -spatial 
data, and recommends that the Department should ensure better coordination between various 
agencies involved in the process to avoid duplicity of efforts, inordinate delays and waste of

information of sensitive and prohibited areas, and recommends the Department to develop fool

1.25  Survey of India (SoI) is developing a platform on which its data assets will be visible to all 
and will be available for sharing among all Government departments and public also. This will 
take care of al l duplicity, delay and waste of resources. Datasets will be shared or made available 
through above platform free of cost to all Government agencies, where as private users will be 
provided data at fair and transparent cost. Government of India data platform  security guidelines 
will be complied with stipulated security auditing of platform and web application.

1.35 In pursuance of above observations, it is submitted that each of the Autonomous 
Institutions  (AIs) has already been suitably counselled to enlist relevant goals /objectives being

into commercial products. The TRC programme is translating scientific discoveries and 
technological inventions into products and services of societal and industrial relevance. TRCs have 
been instrumental in buil ding R&D translation ecosystem by supporting advancements in 
technology readiness levels of background R&D capabilities and intellectual properties, 

9 
 
streamlining multi -stakeholder involvement (including industry -academia partnerships), 
technology out -licensing, setting -up platforms for start -ups, and strengthening state -of-the-art 
R&D infrastructure. Around a dozen of technologies have been transferred to the industries and 
many of them are at different stages of developments for transfer to the industries.  These TRCs 
have already started generating revenues. Few more TRCs are under consideration. 
Recommendation/Observation  
1.38  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should provide the necessary 
funds to the Birbal Sahni Institute to impr ove and upgrade its infrastructure. Further, the 
Department should undertake a thorough assessment of the physical infrastructure of its 
Institutions/Autonomous Bodies and provide all help to strengthen their infrastructure.                                                                                          
          (Para 7.6 ibid)    
Action Taken 
1.39 In pursuance of above observations, it is submitted that the Department is providing 
necessary funds to Autonomous Institutions and administrative assistance to improve and upgrade 
its research and infrastructure. The Department has been providing grants in aid to improve the 
physical infrastructure of its Autonomous Institutions  within the allocated budget. During the 
recent years, new Infrastructure ha ve been created for the Autonomous Institutions  located at 
different parts of the country and many of the infrastructure proposals are under pipeline. 
GROSS EXPENDITURE ON R&D (GERD) 
Recommendation/Observation  
1.40 The Committee recognises the efforts of the Department in promoting R&D activities and 
highlights the importance of a higher allocation of resources in Research and Development 
activities. However, the Committee is concerned with the stagnation and decline of Gross 
Expenditure on R&D as a percentage of GDP.  The Committee cannot stress enough on the urgent 
need to enhance the GERD as a percentage of GDP and, therefore, urges the Department to 
undertake aggressive steps towards promoting private sector investment in Research and 
Development, espec ially since October 2019, companies have been allowed to use Corporate 
Social Responsibility(CSR) funds for contributions towards research.                      (Para 8.2 ibid) 
                                                                                              
Action Taken 
1.41 In various schemes implemented by the Department for augmenting and strengthening of 
research infrastructure in academic institutions, the existing guideline provides for contribution of 
50% share of funds in the recommended budget in project for Private Academic Institutions.  
1.42 National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber Physical Cyber System (NM -ICPS) is 
implemented through 25 Technology Innovation Hubs in the form of Section -8, not for profit 
companies, across the cou ntry. The Companies are to co -partner with Industry, both financially 
and technically, for various activities ranging from R&D to commercialization. All these Hubs are 
encouraged to utilize the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds. Thus, the Mission  is 
working aggressively for promoting private sector contribution to R&D. 
1.43 Under KIRAN programme steps for involvement of companies and using their Corporate 
Social Responsibility (CSR) funds have been taken. IBM, India is involved in Vigyan Jyoti 
Programme and providing its CSR funds to support various activities of the programme.  
1.44 The Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB), a Statutory body of the Department 
has taken significant initiatives towards promoting private sector investment in Research and 

10 
 
Development (R&D). The Scheme, Industry Relevant Research & Development (IRRD) had been 
instituted to target solution driven research to address industry specific problems. The Scheme 
utilizes the expertise available in academic institutions a nd national laboratories to solve industry 
specific problems for the larger benefit of society. 
1.45   In order to further catalyze industry relevant research in academic settings, the Board has 
recently initiated a new programme titled ‘Fund for Industria l Research Engagement (FIRE)’. The 
projects identified under SERB -FIRE shall be jointly designed and implemented by the academic 
partner (which includes a partner from national laboratories/recognized R&D institutions as the 
case may be) and industry. SERB  and Industry share the cost on 1:1 basis.  The SERB has already 
signed Letter of Intent / MoU with some key industry players. 
1.46 The Department, in partnership with Ministry of Education (MoE) , has been implementing 
an initiative called I mpacting Resear ch, I nnovation and Technology (IMPRINT) to address all 
major engineering challenges relevant to India through an inclusive and sustainable mode of 
translational research steered by the top engineering institutions in the country.  The SERB has 
been entrust ed to implement IMPRINT – 2 R&D projects and function as a single window 
clearance system of all the financial requirements of the selected projects. The programme ensures 
mandatory engagement and investment of private industries. 
1.47 SERB has recently ma de call for R&D proposals on SERB Centre for Energy 
Transformation and Storage in three specific areas, namely, Electrochemical energy storage 
systems for micro -grid installations, Technologies for utility -scale high -capacity batteries and 
Transparent photovoltaics for devices and surface integration. In order to boost private investment 
and sustainability, it is mandated that the Centres should ensure (added) funding from non -SERB 
sources such as industry, institution, etc.

Recommendation/Observation  
4.1       The Committee welcomes the creation of a National Research Foundation  to increase the 
resources for Research and Development and strengthening its outreach, although the logic of its 
being managed by the Ministry of Education is not very clear. Such a NRF must focus sharply on 
the natural sciences. Bringing social sciences also under its ambit is not advisable. Since, as stated 
by the Department of Science and Technology, the objectives, structure and processes of the 
proposed NRF  are duplicate or parallel  to some of the existing initiatives in the Ministry of 
Science and Technology, especially DST and DBT, the Committee is of the view that the National 
Research Foundation should work closely with the Ministry of Science and Technology to avoid 
duplication of efforts. The Committee endorses the view of the Department that DST  and DBT be 
included in the NRF Council, to avoid duplication and to bring synergy in all major extra -mural 
support. Further, the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government should strongly consider 
focusing NRF efforts in under -served regions and under -funded areas of research, building 
research capacity of states and the ability of state governments to spend on R&D, and amplifying 
important strategic initiatives of the Ministry of Science and Technology.

SPACE ECOSYSTEM vis-à-vis PARTICIPATION OF PRIVATE SECTOR 
Recommendation/Observation  
1.21 The Committee acknowledges and appreciates the efforts being made by the Department of 
Space to promote the private sector participation in the space ecosystem of the country.  The 
Committee feels that with strategic policy  interventions, the Department can further work towards 
tapping the immense potential of the MSMEs/private sector working in the space sector.                              
The Committee, therefore, welcomes the creation of Indian National Space Promotion a nd 
Authorisation Center (IN-SPACe).  The Committee hopes that the purpose for which IN -SPACe has 
been created, will be achieved and India’s share in the space industry globally will double in the 
next five years with the help of private sector participation.                                                 (Para 8.3)                                                         
 The Committee, however, is of the view that creating a successful public private partnership 
to develop technology for enhanced throughput requirements of satellites and launch vehicles in the 
country is a challenging task, which depends on the convergence of our research in both the 
academia and industry.  The Committee is of the considered view that the efforts of the Department 
for commercialising the space sector further needs to be supplemented by a sound legal and policy 
framework.  The Committee notes that the Department is seized with the task of reforming space 
sector and various policies are being introduced for the purpos e. The Committee urges the 
Department to consult all stakeholders in this process and introduce the Space Activities Bill soon, 
for the effective promotion and regulation of private players in the space sector.        (Para 8.4 ibid) 
 
 

7 
 
Action Taken 
1.22 Department of Space is in the process of implementing space sector reforms announced by 
Government of India. The reforms are aimed at enabling private players to carry out end -to-end 
space activities through promotion and handholding, sharing of ISRO facil ities, expertise and 
technology and also by authorizing and monitoring private sector‟s space activities as per regulatory 
provisions.  
To facilitate these reforms, the existing policies in space domain ha ve been revised and new 
policies are being drafted and processed. A total of 10 sector specific policies are under various 
stages of processing viz; Space Com Policy, Remote Sensing Policy, Technology Transfer Policy, 
Navigation Policy, Human in Space Policy, Space Transportation Policy, Space Exploration Policy, 
Space Situational Awareness policy, Overall National Space Policy and Space FDI Policy.  
In order to address the necessary legal framework, the department is also in the process of 
enacting a National legislation and the draft Space Activities Bill  has completed Public and Legal 
consultations and the draft Bill will be processed for further approvals for inter -ministerial 
consultations. 
Recommendation/Observation  
1.23 The Committee appreciates that the Department has initiated addressing the immedi ate 
requirements from private entities for proceeding with the space activities.  The Committee, 
however, feels that the Department should examine all the pros and cons related with this issue 
threadbare instead of rushing through the process.                                                      (Para 8.5 ibid)                                                                                                             
Action Taken 
1.24 As part of space sector reforms, Government of India has created a Nodal Agency viz Indian 
National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN -SPACe) under DOS for supporting the 
activities of private players in the country.  
However, there is a surge of requirements from private entities for supporting their spac e 
activities. As of now, 36 proposals in various segments including building Launch vehicles, 
building Satellites, providing Satellite services, establishing Ground segments, Research 
Partnerships and providing Mission services were received by the Departm ent and these are under 
various stage of processing.  The proposals include all categories like  large industries, Micro, Small 
and Medium Enterprises ( MSMEs), start ups, new business ventures and academia. A National 
registration mechanism for space objects was implemented and five private satellites were 
registered.  4 MoUs and 2 Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDAs) were signed with private/academic 
entities for sharing t echnical expertise and facilities of ISRO. 5 private satellites were tested at 
ISRO facilities. Handholding by ISRO was undertaken for resolving technical issues of satellites.   
Recommendation/Observation  
1.25 The Committee would also like to highlight the importance and need of developing 
indigenous state -of-the-art technologies, devices and services in order to cater to the emerging 
needs of the society.  Indigenously developed technologies, service, devices, etc. will help the 
Department to reduce its import bill considerably apart from reducing the dependability on 
imports.   It is learnt that approximately 60 -70% of the total requirement of electronic components 
are imported.  It is, therefore, of great sign ificance and importance to have electronic components 
produced indigenously.  It would also generate employment locally.  The Committee hopes that 
opening up the space sector for private entities will further help in achieving indigenisation of these 
technologies, devices and services.                                                                                 (Para 8.6 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.26 The observations of the Committee are noted.

Climate Change in respect of all the eleven recommendations/observations contained in the Three 
Hundred Forty-Sixth Report of the Committee. This has been categorized as follows:-

 Total recommendation– 08 accepted. 
 The Committee is pleased to note that the Ministry has accepted its

Government have not been accepted by the Committee: Para Nos. 4.4
