Government are still awaited: Nil. 
3. The details of the ATR have been analyzed in the succeeding Chapters. 

2  
CHAPTER-I 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
GOVERNMENT 
 
BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 20 20-21 AND ALLOCATION FOR 
the year 2021-22 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.1 The Committee notes the adverse effect of COVID -19 pandemic on the budgetary allocation of 
the Ministry whereby the BE allocation of the Ministry for  the year 2020-21was drastically reduced by 
35% at RE stage, thus resu lting in non -release of funds for all proposed activities mentioned in the 
Annual Plan of Operations (APOs) of various schemes. The Ministry has been able to spend 83% of 
the RE allocation upto 31 st January 2021. The Committee urges the Ministry to optimally utilise the 
funds available with it during remaining part of the year.                        (Para 2.3 of the 346th Report)                                                                                                                                                            
Action Taken 
1.2 All possible efforts were taken to optimally utilise the funds available under the Ministry during 
the FY 2020 -21. The Ministry was able to incur expenditure of Rs.1973.38 crore against the RE 
provisions of Rs.2015.00 crore i.e. 97.93% w.r.t. RE. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 1.3  The Committee notes that the reduction of funds of the Mi nistry at RE - 2020-21 was due to an 
unprecedented situation caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. However, the BE 2021 -22 of the Ministry 
is still less than BE 2020 -21 (Rs.3100 crore) and even BE 2019 -20 (Rs.2954.72). The Ministry has 
indicated that it requires an additional amount of Rs.900 crores during 2021 -22 for its k ey 
schemes/programmes. The Committee recommends that in 2021 -22, the Ministry of Environment, 
Forest and Climate Change should make proactive efforts to ensure that the physical targets of the 
Ministry in respect of its various schemes/programmes are on sc hedule and the allocation made at BE 
is utilised to the maximum, so that it is on a firm footing to seek additional funds at the Supplementary 
and RE stage to achieve its objectives during the year.                                                     (Para 2.6 ibid)                                                                 
 Action Taken 
1.4 The recommendation of the committee has been noted and necessary augmentation in budgetary 
allocation shall be sought at RE stage as per requirement of the scheme. 
 
BUDGETARY SUPPORT & ACTUALLY UTILISED DURING THE LAST THREE YEARS 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.5 The Committee notes the pattern of utilisation of allocated amount by the Ministry during the 
last three financial years and finds the same satisfactory. The Committee also notes that although the 
BE allocation of the Ministry was reduced by nearly Rs.300 crores at RE stage during 2019 - 20, 
indicating a slow start to the schemes in the initial phase, thereby leading to the reduction in 
allocation at the RE stage, the Ministry was able to utilise the allocation fully during that year. The 
Committee also notes that the Ministry has been able to spend 83% of the RE 2020 -21 allocation upto 
31st January 2021, which is satisfactory.                                                                            (Para 3.2 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.6 The observation of the committee regarding slow start to the scheme in the initial phase, thereby 
leading to the reduction in allocation at the RE stage has been noted and the Pro gramme Divisions of 

3  
the Ministry have been asked to make proactive efforts to ensure that the allocation made at BE may be 
utilised to the maximum during first half of the year. 
CONTROL OF POLLUTION 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.7 Further, the Committee strongly recommends the need for transparency in information relating 
to expenditure of ‘Control of Pollution’ scheme, progress of NCAP, and functioning of the Pollution 
Control Boards.                                                                                                             (Para 4.5 ibid)                                                            
Action Taken 
1.8 The recommendation of the Committee has been noted. All the funds under „Control of 
Pollution‟ scheme are being disbursed/monitored under PFMS. Ministry in collaboration with CPCB is 
also developing a web based air quality database management system with dashboard with provision 
for monitoring of NCAP activities.  CP Division of the Ministry follows scrupul ously, in each case the 
observation made by finance wing of the Ministry (IFD) such as production of utilization certificate 
etc. NCAP is a part of umbrella scheme Control of Pollution.  CPCB is a statutory Body of the Ministry 
and SPCBs/PCCs are the body under States/UTs Governments. 
R&D SCHEME FOR CONSERVATION AND DEVELOPMENT  
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.9 The Committee is dismayed to note that during the last three years, the actual expenditure under 
‘R&D Scheme for Conservation and Development’ has been only 16.3%, 35.8% and 23.5%, 
respectively, of the allocated amount. Under utilisation of the funds raises doubts about the 
achievements of the physical targets set under various progr ammes under the scheme too. Facilitating 
research and development and investing for the same are extremely critical. The Committee had dwelt 
upon this issue in its 331 st Report on Demands for Grants 2020 -21 of the Ministry too. However, the 
situation still remains the same. The Committee would like to reiterate its earlier recommendation and 
urge the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change to introspect on the poor usage of funds 
allocated to Research and Development, and take appropriate measures to correct this immediately. 
                                                                                                                                             (Para 5.3 ibid)                                                                                                                            
Action Taken  
1.10 The Ministry has taken serious note of the concern of the Committee regarding low utilization of 
fund under „R&D Scheme for Conservation and Development‟. Low utilization of funds was due to the 
administrative activities for new projects (as decided a online portal for processing the applications for 
R&D Scheme became active in August , 2018 only) and the expenditure in the scheme is being done in 
a systematic manner to use it opti mally. Further, the „R&D Scheme for Conservation and 
Development‟ provides selective support in the form of grant to institutions in the country with 
expertise in identified thematic areas to undertake specific projects on specific areas of concern and 
priority and/or urgency of the Ministry for meeting Ministry‟s objectives of environmental protection 
and conservation of natural resources. Other Central Sector Scheme and Centrally Sponsored Schemes 
of the Ministry have also provided/earmarked fund for Research and Development in concerned fields. 
MAN-ANIMAL CONFLICT 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.11 The Committee is of the view that the cases of man-animal conflict are rising and it still  remains 
an area of concern. There is an urgent need to minimise the instances of man -animal conflict resulting 
in both loss of human and animal life.                                                                             (Para 6.3 ibid) 
 

4  
Action Taken  
1.12 The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has taken following steps to minimize 
the instances of man-animal conflict resulting in both loss of human and animal life 
i. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has issued advisories dated 24th 
December, 2014 and 1st June, 2015, in context of human wildlife conflicts to all the States /UT‟s, 
wherein they have been requested to take proactive steps including exercise of powers under the Wild 
Life (Protection) Act, 1972, for mitigation of human wildlife conflict. 
ii. The Ministry has issued an advisory on payment of ex -gratia in context of human-wildlife conflict 
case of the Chief Wildlife Wardens of all the State Governments/Union Territory Administrations 
dated 10th July, 2020. 
iii. The Ministry has implemented a pilot project on the immuno-contraception as a long term measure 
to control the population of wild animals responsible for damage and destruction of crops, namely wild 
boar, elephant, monkey and nilgai. 
iv. Under Development of Wildlife Habitat (DWH) Scheme there is a provision o f "Management of 
human animal conflict in and around forest areas by  providing ex-gratia compensation to victim, 
support to states in construction of mitigation structure and relocation of villages." 
v. The Ministry has issued advisory on human wildlife conflict on 06.02.2021 after obtaining 
recommendation of the National Board for Wildlife. 
MONITORING OF PLANTATION ACTIVITIES  
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.13 The Committee observes that a year has gone by and  the Committee is still apprehensive on  the 
matter of misappropriation in plantation drives. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of 
Environment, Forest and Climate Change should allay the concerns on this front in a transparent 
manner through audits that can be accessed easily by both public representatives and civil society.  
                                                                                                                                             (Para 7.3 ibid)                                                                                                                                
Action Taken                      
1.14 The Ministry implements two major afforestation schemes which include National Afforestation 
Programme (NAP) and Green India Mission (GIM). The guidelines of these schemes have inherent 
provisions for monitoring and evaluation of the project. 
The National Afforestation Programme (NAP) is implemented through a three tier system involving 
Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs) at Village level, Forest Development Agency (FDAs) 
at Division level and State Forest Development Agency (SFDAs) at State level. The guidelines of the 
scheme provides for concurrent monitoring of the project under the schem e and each project under the 
scheme is monitored by SFDA, FDA and State/UT Forest Department officials through field 
inspections and reports. Besides that SFDAs also carry out independent evaluation of each project. The 
evaluation focuses on people‟s participation, status of regeneration and improvement of vegetation, etc. 
The Green India Mission (GIM) monitors the progress of work through comprehensive monitoring 
framework i.e. on -ground self -monitoring by implementing agencies, field review by an external  
agency; KML file, Photographs, Audit report and Annual progress reports , etc. The Mission has also 
constituted Monitoring Committees for every State to monitor and evaluate Green India Mission 
activities. 
Besides, Eco-development Scheme is implemented in 4 States only, for eco -restoration of difficult or 
inaccessible terrains by Eco Task Force battalions cons tituted by employing ex -servicemen. The 
plantation done by ETF battalions have high survival percentage as t hey are monitored by ex -

5  
servicemen and other officials of the battalions. Besides these , plantations are also monitored by State 
Government officials and also by submission of progress reports, photos, etc. 
 Besides, the inherent provisions in the guidelines of the afforestation schemes, monitoring is also done 
through scrutiny of the proposals submitted by State Forest Development Agency. Each proposal from 
SFDA is required to include photos of the plantation area, geo-coordinates, progress report and 
evaluation reports which are scrutinized in the Ministry. 
In addition, 3rd party independent evaluation of plantation activities is also carried out by the Ministry, 
which includes sample check of plantations taken up by States under different schemes, evaluation of 
plantation activities under schemes  of the Ministry. Besides, the Forest Survey of India also carries out 
biennial survey of forests in the country and gives their assessment about change in forest cover and tree 
cover reflecting the afforestation efforts made to increase green cover in the  country. Government of 
India through Forest Survey of India, Dehradun also maintains the e -Greenwatch portal at which details 
of afforestation of degraded forest land through Compensatory afforestation are provided. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.15 The Committee also expresses its anguish on the issue of non - cooperative and unresponsive 
behaviour of the officials dealing with environmental matters towards the public representatives. Such 
attitude not only puts hurdles in the discharge of their constitut ional obligations but also in their 
accountability to the people. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Environment, Fores st 
and Climate Change, being the nodal central Ministry dealing with these matters, must impress upon 
the State Governments as well as their own officers to sensitise all the concerned authorities to accord 
due courtesy to the public representatives, attend to their grievances, respond to their communications 
and make available the information sought by them.                                                                (Para 7.6)                         
  Action Taken  
1.16 The recommendations of the Committee are duly noted by the Ministry for implementation of 
the suggestion of the Committee. The Ministry places due importance  on resolution of public 
grievances received by it, and endeavors to resolve them in a time -bound manner. It also, provides the 
requisite information to various stakeholders. 

6  
CHAPTER – II 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE 
TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT'S REPLIES 
CONTROL OF POLLUTION 
Recommendation/ Observation 
2.1 The Committee understands that the  Ministry of Environment, Fores  and Climate Change 
utilises the allocation made for ‘Control of Pollution’ under its various schemes and programmes. The 
Committee is of the view that apart from implementing its various schemes and programmes, the 
Ministry needs to innovate and invest in  creating infrastructure for pollution abatement measures 
having sustainable and long -term impact such as installing superchargers for electric vehicles and 
establishing Effective Micro -organism bio -digesters units. Installing super -chargers for electric 
vehicles in cities affected by vehicular pollution will accelerate transition of people from petrol/diesel 
to electric vehicles, thereby reducing vehicular pollution. Similarly, establishing Effective Micro -
organism bio-digesters units after studying learni ngs from pilot projects, will not only help increase 
the efficiency of waste treatment and biogas production in urban areas, but also reduce the problem of 
stubble burning in rural North India, since these bio -digester units can provide effective micro -
organism solution, which, if made available to the farmers at a low cost, can provide them incentives 
to decompose stubble instead of burning it. This will also go a long way in controlling the problem of 
air pollution that severely affects the Indo-Gangetic plains every year.  (Para 4.6 of the 346th Report)                                                                                                                                           
 Action Taken 
2.2 Electric Vehicles and bio-decomposers are the policy issues being handled by the Ministry of 
Power and Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare respectively. Charging infrastructure for 
Electric Vehicles guidelines and standard was issued by the Ministry of Power vide their circular dated 
01.10.2019. However, this Ministry being mandated for healthy and safe  Environment of the country, 
always monitors, guides and makes air pollution mitigation strategy with all other stakeholders. 
Further, MoEF&CC is the nodal agency for monitorin g of progress made by 42 million plus cities 
receiving grant under Million Plus Challenge Fund (MCF), as per recommendation of Fifteenth 
Finance Commission for improvement of air quality. MoEF&CC has included development of such 
charging infrastructure as an essential component of performance assessment parameter for utilization 
of grant under MCF. Other Non -attainment cities are also being encouraged to incorporate this aspect 
in their city action plan for combating air pollution. 
MONITORING OF PLANTATION ACTIVITIES  
Recommendation/ Observation 
2.3 The Committee expresses its deep concern and dismay that the Supplementary ATR on the above 
issue of CAMPA fund has not been submitted by the Ministry to the Committee much beyond the 
promised timeline. The Committee expects the Ministry to furnish the Supplementary ATR within the 
next two weeks.                                                                                                                   (Para 7.5 ibid) 
Action Taken  
2.4 National Authority under the Ministry has examined the further recommendation of the 
Committee made in their Report No. 339 regarding issue under CAMPA of enhancing synergy 
amongst its different schemes and programmes related to improvement/expansion of  forest and tree 
cover including restoration of degraded forests which is one of the major objectives of the Green India 
Mission and in this regard conveyed the following factual positions:  
(i) The Compensatory Afforestation Fund (CAF) or CAMPA fund is utiliz ed solely for the purpose 
of mitigating the impact of loss of tree cover, forest land, wildlife habitat and ecological services 

7  
rendered by the forests. Hon‟ble Supreme Court of India has decided that this fund is not a part of 
general revenue of the Union, of the States or of the Consolidated Fund of India. This is echoed in the 
CAF Act, 2016, which provides for establishment of two special funds under the Public Account of 
States and under the Public Account of India, namely State Compensatory Afforestati on Funds (State 
Funds) and National Compensatory Aff orestation Fund (National Fund)  respectively, for crediting the 
CAF in the 90:10 ratios. 
(ii) The funding mechanism for implementing the centrally sponsored schemes of the Ministry on 
afforestation (Green India Mission and National Afforestation Programme) provides for sharing cost of 
these projects between the Centre and State/UT in 60:40 or 90:10 ratios (as per GOI norms). As of 
now, the cost is borne by the Centre as well as by the States/UTs from their resp ective consolidated 
funds. On the other hand, the activities undertaken from the State Fund or National Fund of CAF are 
fully funded by the respective Public Accounts . Rule 230 (1) of General Financial Rules, 2017 on 
„Principles and Procedure for award of Grants-in-aid‟ provides that “The Institution or Organization 
seeking Grants -in-aid should also certify that it has not obtained or applied for grants for the same 
purpose or activity from any other Ministry or Department of the Government of India or Stat e 
Government”. Further, under no circumstances, mixing of the monies received towards Net Present 
Value ( NPV) or interest accrued on the monies in the State Fund is allowed with any other State 
budget either for capital or spill over works and the works un dertaken under this rule shall be on 
standalone basis and there shall not be any duplication of permitted works under different components. 
In addition, monies collected towards any site -specific schemes including Compensatory Afforestation 
(CA) etc., are to be used as per site specific schemes approved at the time of approval of diversion of 
forest land under Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980. Because of the above provisions and two different 
funding mechanisms, funding under the CSS cannot be augmented with  State Fund or National Fund 
established under the Public Accounts. 
(iii) As per the mechanism provided in the CAF Act, 2016 and CAF Rules, 2018, the Executive 
Committee of the State Authority of the respective States/UTs formulates and submits annual plan of 
operations to be Steering Committee of the State Authority for its concurrence. The Steering 
Committee of the State Authority scrutinizes and approves the annual plan of operations at the State 
level and thereafter sends the same to the Executive Committee o f the National Authority for final 
approval. It is to be noted here that the Executive Committee of the State Authority also includes one 
representative from the Departments of Environment, Finance, Planning, Rural Development, 
Revenue, Agriculture, Tribal  Development, Panchayati Raj, Science and Technology each as its 
members. Besides, two eminent non -government organizations, two representatives of district level 
Panchayati Raj Institutions, an expert on tribal matters or a representative of tribal commun ity, Nodal 
Officer, State Forest Development Agency (SFDA) are also included. Similarly, the Steering 
Committee of the State Authority constituted under the chairmanship of the Chief Secretary also 
includes Principle Secretaries of the Departments dealing with Forests, Environment, Finance, 
Planning, Rural Development, Revenue, Agriculture, Tribal Development, Panchayati Raj, Science 
and Technology, Nodal Officer, SFDA and an expert on tribal matters or a representative of tribal 
community as its members. T hese arrangements at State/UT ensure that synergy amongst different 
schemes and programmes related to improvement/expansion of forest and tree cover at State/UT level 
is achieved. 
(iv) The National Fund consists of only 10% of the CAF an d is to be used judiciously and 
strategically to improve the efficacy of the State Fund, which is a much larger fund. Section 5(b) of the 
CAF Act, 2016 provides for specific purposes for which the monies under National Fund can be 
utilized. This fund is ut ilized for meeting: (a) The non -recurring and recurring expenditure for 
management of the National Authority, including salaries and allowances payable to its officers and 
employees, (b) the expenditure incurred on monitoring and evaluation of works execut ed by the 
National and each State Authority, (c) The expenditure incurred on specific schemes approved by the 

8  
Governing Body of the National Authority. Such scheme would include any institute, society, centre of 
excellence in the field of forest and wildlife, pilot schemes, standardization of codes and guidelines and 
such other related activities for the forestry and wildlife sector. Consequently, more than fourteen 
proposals submitted by different divisions of the Ministry and State/UTs at an outlay of Rs. 965.31 
crore (approximately) have been carefully selected and are being funded as per Section 5(b) (iii) of 
CAF Act, 2016 for meeting the expenditure incurred on these specific schemes after the approval of 
the National Authority. These include Implementin g “ the Central Asian Flyway National Action Plan 
with Special Focus on Preparation of Site -Specific Activity Plan, Capacity Building and Developing 
Bird Sensitivity app for Setting up of Wind Energy and Species Action Plan”, “Proposal of Estimation 
of Economic Losses in Real Term Per Hectare Basis Due to Forest Fire in Uttarakhand and Madhya 
Pradesh”, “Execution of Readiness Activities for implementation of REDD+ in India”, “Strengthening 
of Forestry Research for Ecological Sustainability Productivity Enha ncement”, “National Programme 
for Conservation and Development of Forest Genetic Resources : Pilot project on „Creation of Centre 
of Excellence on Forest Genetic Resources‟, “Monitoring Protocol for Plantations and Assets created 
by State Forest Department s from Compensatory Afforestation Fund”, “Preparation of DPR with 
LiDAR Survey for one pilot watershed in forest area of each State/UT”, “Endangered Species 
Recovery Programme for Dugong, Dolpin, Great Indian Bustard & Sangai”, “Management of 
PARIVESH Portal”, to name a few. Thus, at the national level, these specific schemes under National 
Fund of CAF complement the other schemes and programme for improvement/expansion of forest and 
tree funding during 2020-21. 

9  
CHAPTER – III 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE 
GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE 
CONTROL OF POLLUTION 
Recommendation/ Observation 
3.1 The Committee notes that the ‘Control of Pollution’ scheme is to be implemented through various 
Central and State Government agencies. The Committee is of the view that although there may be 
different fund contributors to various implementation agencies under the scheme, there should be a 
central mechanism for coordination of various Central and State agencies and ensuring accountability 
through monitoring of the progress of the works undertaken. Further, capacity building should be 
undertaken at the municipal level to ensure implementation of The National Clean Air Programme 
(NCAP). These mea sures are critical for the successful execution of the scheme. The Committee 
recommends that the grant made available by recommendation of 15 th Finance Commission for 
installation of systems to monitor air quality must be prioritised by the Ministry in the  smaller cities 
and towns that are often neglected, and suffer from a lack of quality data on air pollution.

CHAPTER-I 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
GOVERNMENT 
BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2020 -21 AND ALLOCATION 
FOR 2021-22 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.1 The Committee notes that the Ministry, under its Capital Budget, was allocated Rs.74.90 
crore in RE 2020 -21 against the budgeta ry allocation of Rs.172 crore in BE 2020 -21.  The 
Committee further notes that the Ministry has been given Rs.163 crore in BE 2021 -22 which is 
Rs. 57.79 crore more than the actual expenditure of Rs.105.21 crore during the year 2019 -20 in 
the same category. The Committee urges the Department to complete all its programme s/projects 
envisaged for the year 2021 -22, and fully utilise the allocation of Rs.172 crore in BE 2020 -21, 
especially since the trend of the last several years even before COVID -19 pandemic has been of 
actual expenditure being lower than the revised estimates.                 (Para 2.3of the 347th Report) 
Action Taken 
1.2 Noted for compliance.  Due to the austerity measures , due to Covid pandemic, the overall 
budget of the Ministry was reduced by Rs. 770 crore from Rs. 2070 crore to Rs.1300 crore at RE 
stage.  Accordingly, at RE stage allocation u nder Capital was reduced to Rs. 74.90 crore against 
allocation o f Rs. 172 crore under Capital in BE 2020 -21.  The Ministry has incurred an 
expenditure of Rs. 69.70 crore (93.1% of RE) during 2020 -21 under Capital.  The Ministry could 
not fully utilize Rs. 74.90 crore (RE 2020-21) as Central Public Work Department  (CPWD) was 
unable to fully utilize the funds authorised to them to carry out Major works assigned to them by 
India Meteorological Department  (IMD) and Centre for Marine Living Resources & Ecology 
(CMLRE) and slow progress of boundary wall construction by the contractor at Mandapam for 
National Centre for Coastal Research (NCCR) Field Centre. 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.3 The Committee further opines that the Ministry should prepare a blueprint highlighting 
the avenues that can be explored by the Ministry to generate revenue during the next 5 years, to 
reduce the pressure on the budget of the Ministry, and accomplish its critical expansion plans.  
                                 (Para 2.11ibid)                                              
Action Taken 
1.4 Noted for compliance. The Ministry will come out with a blueprint highlighting the 
avenues that can be explored to generate revenue during the next 5 years. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.5 The Committee recommends that the Ministry scale up holding various seminars, training 
sessions, etc. online, wherever feasible, to help the Ministry to save its financial resources, 
whereas the money saved could be better utilised for its R&D activities or other equally important 
priorities.                                                                                                                    (Para 2.12 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.6 Noted for compliance. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.7 The Committee recommends that the Ministry should take immediate corrective remedial 
action in the matter and impresses upon all the related government/private bodies to initiate the 
process of clearing their dues at the earliest.                                                        (Para 2.14 ibid)    
                                                                                 
 

3 
 
Action Taken 
1.8 The matter of over dues of payment has been taken up with the top level of Airports 
Authority of India (AAI) and D.O. letters dated 15.04.2020 and 16.12.2020 have been written by 
DGM, India Meteorological Department ( IMD) to the Chairman, AAI.  To further remove the 
lagging in the recovery of dues from AAI in future, the IMD is in process of signing a new MOU 
with AAI.  In this MOU, a new mechanism has been proposed whereby IMD will charge 4.5% of 
Route Navigation Facility Charges ( RNFC) of AAI.   Further, it is being insisted that before 
signing the New MOU, AAI has to clear all dues of IMD.   It is also mentioned here that in 
compliance with audit observation, IMD has also requested AAI to include the penalty clause in 
the MOU for delay i n payment towards the cost of Aviation Met services being provided to AAI 
by IMD. It is also mentioned in the new MOU that the bill will be raised on a monthly basis by 
the IMD. 
UMBRELLA SCHEMES OF MINISTRY OF EARTH SCIENCES 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.9 The above data suggests that the overall financial performance of the umbrella schemes of 
the Ministry has been satisfactory.  However, under the Seismology and Geosciences (SAGE)  
scheme, the Ministry has spent only 65% of its allocated fund upto January, 2021 during the year 
2020-21.  The Committee urges the Ministry to optimally utilise the unspent funds during the 
remaining part of the Financial Year 2020-21.                                                          (Para 3.4 ibid)                                                                                                                                                                                         
Action Taken 
1.10 Against Rs.39 crore allocated at RE stage under SAGE during 2020 -21, an amount of Rs. 
38.74 crore has been spent during the year. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.11 The Committee also notes that though the overall budgetary allocation under the umbrella 
Schemes of the Ministry in BE 2021 -22 is little less than the allocation of BE 2020 -21, it is 
hopeful that the Ministry will make earnest efforts to ensure that the funds allocated in BE 2021 -
22 will be optimally utilised.   The Committee also hopes that t he Ministry, with the help of its 
periodic reviews of the financial and physical performance of these Schemes, will strive hard to 
achieve the targets set for the year 2021-22.                              (Para 3.5 ibid)                                                      
Action Taken 
1.12 The Ministry thanks the Committee and has noted the advice for compliance.   Half yearly 
reviews are regularly undertaken under the Chairmanship of Secretary to review the financial and  
physical performance of each of the schemes.   In addition, periodic reviews are done every month 
to ensure judicious use of the budget to ensure un -interrupted service for operational activities of 
the Ministry. The Ministry has incurred an expenditure o f ₹259 crore which is 13.65% of BE as 
on 10th June 2021.  
AUTONOMOUS BODIES 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.13 The Committee finds the overall fund utilisation by the autonomous institutions during the 
years 2018-19, 2019 -20 and 2020 -21 to be satisfactory which has been to the tune of 99.31%, 
98.90% and 84.86% respectively. The Committee, however, feels that the financial performance of 
National Centre for Earth Science Studies (NCESS) could have been better during the year 2020 -
21, whereas it utilised only 71.20% of the allocated amount upto 31.01.2021.         (Para 4.3 ibid)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
Action Taken 
1.14 The expenditure in 2020 -21 (71.2% as per the table) till 31.01.2021 was arrived at based 
on expenditure of Rs. 8.90 crore which is likely to be a mid -year figure. The expe nditure of the 
full year is ₹12.50 crore which is 100% of the RE of Rs.12.50 crore. 

4 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.15 The Committee has noted with concern the non -utilisation of grants amounting to Rs. 
173.67 crore received by National Institute of Ocean Technology ( NIOT) from the Ministry and 
blockage of Government funds to the tune of ₹16.06 crore in respect of R&D prog rammes by 
NCESS.  The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to take immediate remedial action 
in the matter and ensure that the funds being made available to the autonomous bodies under the 
control of the Ministry are properly utilised for the purpose envisaged.                   (Para 4.5 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.16 The Ministry will strive hard to increase the efficiency of fund utilization by various 
Institutes in the coming years. 
DEEP OCEAN MISSION 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.17 The Committee notes the various components and proposed activities envisaged by the 
Ministry under its Deep Ocean Mission and the funds required to realise the intended benefits of 
the Mission.  The Committee acknowledges that this Mission will not only st rengthen country’s 
position in the Indian Ocean region, but envisages exploration of minerals, energy and marine 
diversity of the underwater world, a vast part of which still remains unexplored.  Since this 
Mission is an     inter-ministerial Mission where various other Ministries and Departments of the 
Government of India such as  Indian Space Research Organisation  (ISRO), Defence Research & 
Development Organisation ( DRDO), Council of Scientific & Industrial Research ( CSIR), 
Department of  Biotechnology (DBT), etc. also on board with the Ministry of Earth Sciences.  The 
Committee urges all these wings of the Government to work in tandem to make this Mission a 
success.    The Ministry has indicated a requirement of ₹400 crore for the Deep Ocean Mission 
(DOM).  It is of the utmost importance that the Mission is adequately funded by the Government 
with timely availability of the funds to facilitate the Mission in realising its intended goals in a 
systematic and time bound manner.                                                                            (Para 5.2 ibid)  
Action Taken 
1.18 The Ministry thanks the Committee for its support to the Deep Ocean Mission. The Deep 
Ocean Mission, India‟s ambitious plan to explore and harness deep -oceanic resources was 
approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs  on 16/06/2021.  The program w ill be 
implemented at an estimated cost of  ₹4,077 crore over five years in a phased manner.   MoES 
shall coordinate with the institutes mentioned above and also with academic organisations and 
industry partners for the efficient timely execution of the Mission. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.19 The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Finance should provide the 
requisite funds at the RE stage to the Ministry so that the Mission is successful.      (Para 5.3 ibid)                                                                                           
Action Taken 
1.20 The Ministry will seek the required funds through the 2 nd Supplementary Demands for 
Grants 2021-22. 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.21 The Committee acknowledges both the strategic importance of India’s presence in the 
Arctic, the Antarctic, and the Southern Indian Ocean, and the tangible impact of scientific 
research carried out there for the nation, especially on climate change and the Indian monsoon.  
The Committee also notes how China has invested both resources and scientific manpower in 
these regions.  The Committee therefore recommends that the Ministry prepare a realistic plan for 
its expansion in the next 5 years, including capita l expenditure for the acquisition of polar 
research vessel and aircraft, and scientific manpower in the Arctic, Antarctic and the South 

5 
 
Indian Ocean.  The Committee urges the Ministry to impress upon the Ministry of Finance to 
provide requisite funds for the same in a timely manner.                                           (Para 5.5 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.22 Ministry thanks the Committee for acknowledging the strategic importance of India‟s 
presence in the Polar Region and impact of scientific research carried out there.  The realistic plan 
for expansion in the next 5 years is including in the Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) memo 
for continuing of Polar and Cryosphere Research (PACER) scheme.  It also includes the proposal 
of creation of scientific m anpower, both permanent and temporary, for Polar Science. Since the 
proposed EFC is for continuing program, the capital expenditure for acquisition of Polar Research 
Vessel (PRV) and renovation/reconstruction of Maitri Station will be taken up as a sep arate EFC 
for Cabinet approval.  MoES will pursue with the Ministry of Finance to provide requisite funds 
for the same. 
  

6

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT 
DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT'S REPLIES 
BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2020 -21 AND ALLOCATION 
FOR 2021-22 
Recommendation/Observation 
2.1 The Committee observes that though the Department utilise d Rs. 1,121.86 crore till 
January, 2021 against Rs. 1,300 crore in RE 2020 -21 which is 86.29% utilisation, however, the 
utilisation of funds in terms of BE 2020 -21 allocation of Rs. 2070 crore has only been to the tune

Recommendation/ Observation

about its absolute bare minimum requirement of additional funds in order to sustain its key 
programmes.                                                                                                              (Para 2.10 ibid)  
Action Taken 
2.4 The Ministry thanks the Committee and has noted the advice for compliance.  A letter was 
sent by Secretary MoES to Secretary , Expenditure on 15th April 2021, appraising the requirement

Finance (MoF).

GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE 
BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2020-21 AND ALLOCATION

Recommendation/ Observation 
3.1 The Committee while making note of the activities/road map prepared by the Ministry for 
the Year 2021 -22 hopes that the Ministry will prioritise its activities according to the actual

3.3 The Ministry has merely thanked the Committee and  has not furnished any action

4. DELEGATION OF ENHANCED POWERS FOR  RE-APPROPRIATION OF 
FUNDS TO SECRETARY, DEPARTMENT OF ATOMIC ENERGY 
4.1 During the meeting , the Department apprised the Committee that a t present there are 
restrictions for re -appropriating funds from “Major Works” to any other primary  units like 
“Minor Works”, “Repairs & Maintenance”, “Tools & Plants”, etc.   It was further brought to the 

7 
 
 
notice of the Committee that presen tly the powers of re -appropriation for “Administrative 
Expenses” (viz. under the primary units salaries, wages, travel expenses, etc.) is  limited to 25% 
or Rs. 1 crore, whichever is less.  The Department, accordingly, proposed that full powers may 
be given to the Secretary, Department of Atomic Energy, for re-appropriation of above expenses 
within the same grant which will enable the Department to utilize the budgetary grant to the 
optimum level. 
4.2 The Committee takes note of the proposal and feels that proper care must be taken 
in the matter by the Department  without losing sight of financial prudence.  Granting 
power for re -appropriation of the above mentioned expenses to the Secretary may on the 
one hand solve the problems being faced by the Department but on the other hand this will 
also bring greater amount of responsibility and accountability so as to ensure strict 
adherence to the relevant rules and guidelines laid down for the purpose.                                            
In view of the proposal submitted by the Department, the Committee recommends that full 
powers may be given to the Secretary, Department of Atomic Energy, for re -appropriation 
of „Administrative Expenses‟. The Committee sincerely fee ls that granting such powers for 
re-appropriation would surely help the Department  to make optimum utilisation of the 
budgetary allocations made.

6. CANCER CARE IN THE COUNTRY – ROADMAP FOR FUTURE 
6.1 Responding to the query of the Committee about the availability of cancer care  facilities 
in various parts of the country with specific reference to Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, 
North Karnataka and South Rajasthan , it was informed  by the Department  that the Tata 
Memorial Centre  (TMC) has already functional centres at Mumbai,  Navi Mumbai, Varanasi, 
Guwahati, Sangrur, Vizag, and Muzaffarpur.   Centres at Mullanpur and augmented services at 
Vizag would be functional later this year.  Sharing the plans and suggestions for the States where 
cancer care is not readily available , the following was submitted for the perusal of the 
Committee:- 
(i) It was submitted that Tata Trusts has initiated construction o f the Cancer Hospital 
at Ranchi, Jharkhand which would be completed by July , 2022 and  TMC is 
providing technical support as well as training for the staff.   TMC has a unit at 
Muzaaffarpur also which can support this initiative. 
(ii) It was suggested that the facility at AIIMS, Raipur could be upgraded to function 
as a Hub.  AIIMS, Raipur already has an Oncology Department which can be 
supported and expanded.  TMC would be able to provide technical assistance and 
support, if necessary.  In addition, BALCO Cancer Centre is in existence already 
and TMC has been providing technical support and it should be completed in 18 
months.  
(iii) It was brought to the notice of the Committee that senior faculty from 
TMC had visited the North Bengal Medical College and Hospital, Siliguri  to 
assess the oncology services there and supported the construction and made 
departmental recommendations .  TMC would be providing continued technical 
support and training for this centre. 
(iv) TMC is supporting the temple trust at Mantralayam to develop a  cancer facility in 
Mantralayam which is at the intersection of three States – (i) North -East 
Karnataka; (ii) Telangana; and South Maharashtra. 
(v) TMC could develop a cancer facility at Karwar which would serve the population 
of North-West Karnataka and Goa, both of which currently lack a cancer 
centre. 
(vi) TMC could develop a cancer facility at or nearby Kota  as there are no cancer 
centres in this region and currently patients from South Rajasthan travel to 
Ahmedabad for cancer treatment. 
(vii) TMC is in advanced stage s of planning a cancer hub at the National Institute of 
Science Education and Research (NISER) campus near Bhubaneswar in Odisha.  
This will be built with partial support from Tata Trusts as well as DAE. 
6.2 The Committee was also apprised by the Department that o ne of the most important 
aspects to be addressed is the availability of qualified and trained human resource in all these 
facilities, which are currently not available.   It is important to make the Homi  Bhabha National 
Institute an  “Institute of National Importance” to enable the existing TMC centres at various 
States to start super specialty courses in oncology.  This would ensure that there is convergence 
of human resource with the development of these cancer centres. 
6.3 The Committee appreciates the efforts being made by theTata Memorial Centre  
(TMC) to reach out to the underserved areas of the country so as to ensure that adequate 
cancer care facilities are made available in these areas.  It is also heartening to note that the 

9 
 
 
progress achieved by the TMC in this direction would start showing concrete results in 
times to come. The Committee  feels that the efforts of the TMC further need to be 
supplemented financially for which availability of adequate funds holds the key  to success.  
Therefore, it is imperative to  make available the required funds to the TMC through the 
Department of Atomic Energy  for this cause. The Committee is happy that in BE 2022 -23, 
the Central Government has allocated Rs.700.00 crore for cancer care, education and 
research. The Committee, accordingly, hopes that the TMC would make best use of the 
allocated funds and, if required, the Department would seek additional funds as well in 
order to realise the objectives envisioned for the year 2022-23.   
6.4 The Committee firmly believes that merely having physical infrastructure in place 
alone would not yield the desired results  and it is, therefore, of the utmost importance  and 
great significance  that these facilities are equipped with qualified and trained  human 
resource as well.  Therefore, availability of qualified and trained human resources is 
pivotal in the success of these facilities.   
6.5 The Committee has, accordingly, been given to understand by the Department that  
making the „Homi Bhabha National Institute‟ an “Institute of National Importance” would 
enable the existing  TMC centres at various States to start super specialty courses in 
oncology which would further ensure the convergence of human resource with the 
development of these cancer centres.   
6.6 The Committee in order to address the issue of availability of skilled workforce to 
operate these facilities, finds it appropriate that necessary policy interventions are brought 
out by TMC through the Department of Atomic Energy to declare the „Homi Bhabha 
National Institute‟ as an “Institute of National Importance” .  The Committee, therefore, 
recommends the Department to make necessary efforts in the matter.   
 
  

10 
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS-AT A GLANCE 
OVERALL BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR   2021-22 (BE, RE & 
ACTUAL EXPENDITURE) AND ALLOCATION FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2022-23 
 The Committee hopes that the Department would make earnest efforts and make 
optimum utilisation of the budgetary support provided for the year 2021 -22 in the 
remaining period of the current financial year.                                                           (Para 2.3) 
 The Committee on the basis of the figures provided by the Department in response 
to a query observes that the Department was allotted Rs. 27.15 crore in BE 2021 -22 under 
the component „Heavy Water Production Facility‟ which was increased exponentially to 
Rs. 212.86 crore  at RE stage. The Committee is constrained to note that even though 
exponential allocation was made to the Department at RE stage, the utilisation of the 
Department has been to the tune of Rs. 52.53 crore only, upto January, 2022.                                   
The Committee takes serious note of this under -utilisation of the budgetary support by the 
Department and, accordingly, desires the Department to furnish the detailed reasons which 
have led to such poor utilisation of funds.                                                                     (Para 2.4) 
 The Committee also takes cognizance of the overall under -utilisation of the 
budgetary funds provided to the Department for the Public Sector Undertakings 
particularly under Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) and Bharatiya 
Nabhikaya Vidyut N igam Limited (BHAVINI) under the administrative control of the 
Department. The Committee is pained to note that the Department could not make full 
utilisation of the funds made available for NPCIL; and BHAVINI where the Department 
could utilise 35.25 per c ent; and 38.03 per cent, respectively under these components.  The 
Committee, therefore, recommends the Department to apprise the Committee of the 
detailed reasons for such under-utilisation of funds.                                                   (Para 2.5) 
 The Committee is also dismayed to note that zero utilisation of funds was made 
under Uranium Corporation of India Limited (UCIL), which was allocated Rs. 21.70 crore 
at RE stage 2021 -22.  The Committee would, therefore, like to be informed about the  
reasons due to which zero utilisation of funds was made by the Department.          (Para 2.6) 
 The Committee takes a serious note of the cut in the budgetary allocation of the 
Department of Atomic Energy in BE 2022 -23 and its likely impact on the activit ies of the 
Department.  The Committee also notes with concern that out of the total reduction of     
Rs. 8,177.12 crore, Rs. 3,318.50 crore is under revenue budget and Rs. 4,858.63 crore under 
the capital budget.                                                                                                         (Para 2.10) 
 The Committee further notes that the Department would need additional funds to 
ensure that its R&D activities along with other major importa nt activities are not 
negatively impacted.  The Committee, therefore, desires the Department to prepare a 
detailed note on the additional fund requirement and impress upon the Ministry of Finance 
for the same. The Committee also hopes that the Department w ould make sincere efforts to 
utilise the budgetary support given for the year 2022 -23 optimally and strive hard to 
achieve the envisaged targets both physically and financially.                                  (Para 2.11)   
 
 

11 
 
 
FLEET MODE REACTORS 
 The Committee takes note of the progress achieved by the Department with regard 
to construction of ten indigenous 700 MW Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) in 
Fleet mode.  The Committee learns that moving of reactors from „pre -project stage‟ (which 
also includes excavation), to „under construction stage‟ is marked by the event of placement 
of First Pour of Concrete (FPC) and based on the present status of projects,                                        
FPC of Kaiga 5&6 is expected in 2023; FPC of GHA VP 3 & 4; MBRAPP 1 to 4 is expected

the timeline fixed for movement of these above mentioned reactors from „pre-project stage‟

adopted towards any kind of procedural delay.                                                           (Para 3.8)

Department to furnish a detailed note containing the list of the institutions supported by 
the Department during the last five years; specific number of grant under which that are 
covered and the amount of financial support provided to them by the Department.

 The Committee appreciates the efforts being made by the  Tata Memorial Centre

research. The Committee, accordingly, hopes that the TMC would make best use of the 
allocated funds and, if required, the Department would seek additional funds as well in 
order to realise the objectives envisioned for the year 2022-23.                                  (Para 6.3) 
 The Committee firmly believes that merely having physical infrastructure in place 
alone would not yield the desired results and it is, therefore, of the utmost importance and 
great significance that these facilities are equipped with qualified and trained human 
resource as well.  Therefore, availability of qualified and trained human resources is 
pivotal in the success of these facilities.                                                                          (Para 6.4) 
 The Committee has, accordingly, been given to understand by the Department that 
making the „Homi Bhabha National Institute‟ an “Institute of National Importance” would 
enable the existing TMC centres at various States to start super specialty courses in 
oncology which would  further ensure the convergence of human resource with the 
development of these cancer centres.                                                                             (Para 6.5) 
 The Committee in order to address the issue of availability of skilled workforce to 
operate these facilities, finds it appropriate that necessary policy interventions are brought 
out by TMC through the Department of Atomic Energy to declare the „Homi Bhabh a 
National Institute‟ as an “Institute of National Importance”.  The Committee, therefore,

7. BIOREMIDIATION – FUTURE OF INDIA‟S WASTE MANAGEMENT  
7.1 The Committee, keeping in view the urgent need to treat urban and rural waste and 
remedy the hazards of landfills, sought information about the initiatives of the Department with 
regards to treatment of waste through Biotechnological interventions. The Department submitted 
before the Committee that it has developed various technology platforms to convert different 
solid, liquid and gaseous wastes into renewable fuels, energy and value added products. The 
Department informed that Landfill Leachate is a major source of pollutants and pathogens which 
are lethal for public and environmental health. Treatment of leachate is also mandatory to 
mitigate the risk of the spread of AMR and pathogens in the environment and community. 
7.2 The Committee was informed that the Department has supported waste to energy 
demonstration plants with capacity between 500 Kg/ Day to 10 tons/day, in Telangana, Gujarat, 
and Goa, where organic waste (vegetable market waste, kitchen/hotel waste, organic fraction of 
MSW) has successfully converted to energy. Following biotechnological interventions could be 
made for management of sanitary landfills- 
(i) Anaerobic Digestion, Composting and Bioremediation 
(ii) Recovery of fuel in terms of Methane from stored organic waste 
(iii) Leachate treatment to convert it to compost 
(iv) Risk mitigation for AMR, pathogens spread to community 
7.3 The Committee enquired from the Department, whether bioremediation solutions can be 
implemented at giant sanitary landfills such as the Ghazipur and Bhalswa landfill in Delhi. The 
Committee also probed whether biotechnology can be used for the treatment of waste effluents 
and cleaning of rivers. The Department submitted in a written reply that Bioremediation is a 
natural process that may be a solution for the restoration of organic C arbon Contaminated sites 
including soil/water. In the Bioremediation process, secondary pollutants will not be 
generated. Department of Biotechnology is supporting Research, development and 
demonstration projects on remediation and reclamation of xenobioti c pollutants, degraded soil 
reclamation, oil -based soil contaminants, dye degradation and industrial wastewater, tannery 
waste, etc.  
7.4 The Department informed that the f ollowing focused interventions for waste management 
and pollutant removal are being focused on- 
(i) Phytoremediation, Algal Bioremediation,  
(ii) Microbial-Bioremediation/Geomicrobial bioremediation;  
(iii) Microbial degradation of dumpsite leachate, and, 
(iv) Biologically assisted treatment for crude oil pollutants;  
(v) Waste paper recycling, Bio-mineralization;  
7.5 The Committee, given the potential applications of Biotechnological interventions in 
finding scalable and sustainable solutions to waste treatment, enquired whether Bioremediation 
can prove to be the future. The Department replied that Bioremediation is a futuristic technology 

13 
 
 
in resolving the current and upcoming challenges for cleaner and productive management of 
waste including sanitary landfills and degradation of pollutants in India vis-à-vis mitigating the 
impact of associated climate change. Hence, these technologies may be promoted for scale up to 
provide environment friendly and sustainable solutions. 
7.6 The Committee observes the efforts of the Department in promotion of research and 
development of technological platforms towards finding solutions for waste treatment. The 
Committee therefore recommends that the Department should promote its efforts in a 
holistic manner and involve other stakeholders as well so that the country can take lead in 
using c heap, effective and environmentally sustainable methods in dealing with the 
problem of waste treatment and management.

implemented in the economically and socially backward regions. The Committee 
recommends that the Department should evolve a more  inclusive approach in selection of 
regions. Without the inclusion of those regions, which require scientific interventions and 
support as a stepping stone towards a path to prosperity and better life, the true aim of 
such societal development initiatives cannot be achieved.                                           (Para 6.6)   
 The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department to evolve a policy of 
equitable distribution of resources/initiatives, so that the under -served regions of the 
country, which ha ve till date been, devoid of support from scientific institutions/initiatives 
of the Department of Biotechnology get the much needed push.                                 (Para 6.7)   
BIOREMIDIATION – FUTURE OF INDIA‟S WASTE MANAGEMENT  
 The Committee observes the efforts of the Department in promotion of research and 
development of technological platforms towards finding solutions for waste treatment. The 
Committee therefore recommends that the Department should promote its efforts in a 
holistic manner and involve other stakeholders as well so that the country can take lead in 
using cheap, effective and environmentally sustainable methods in dealing with the 
problem of waste treatment and management.                                                             (Para 7.6)
